findings.text: VCPU load entry selects confidential and conventional paths by VCPU type, delegating to the matching loader and returning without further work on the confidential path.
Conventional VCPU load optionally narrows the pause-loop exiting window when the VCPU was scheduled out and guest pausing is inactive, then loads control state and refreshes posted interrupt state.

Secondary execution tuning is conditional on host capability for the named feature; when present, guest capability decides the requested setting and a helper applies either enable or exiting semantics.

Processor identifier synchronization prefers single-context invalidation when hardware offers it, otherwise uses global invalidation for nonzero identifiers, and performs no operation for identifier zero in the single case.
Invalidation operand passed to hardware combines a sixteen bit identifier plus reserved space with a guest address, issued with an extent selector distinguishing single versus all contexts.

Posted interrupt load skips work when virtual APIC support is off or local APIC is emulated elsewhere; otherwise it handles wakeup cleanup, destination refresh on migration, notification vector restore, suppress-notification clearing, and outstanding-bit promotion.

Posted interrupt load serializes wakeup-list removal against scheduler and wakeup paths by taking the previous processor wakeup lock under disabled interrupts, and updates the descriptor control word atomically with retry.

Confidential VCPU load always refreshes posted interrupt state first, then returns early if still on the same processor or if hardware key identity is unassigned, otherwise flushes and links tracking state under interrupts disabled with ordering against disassociation.

Dirty logging update rejects confidential VCPUs, requires page-modification logging support, and sets or clears the corresponding secondary execution bit according to whether any memory slot is currently tracked for dirty logging.

Switch-to-guest preparation dispatches by VCPU type; both variants run once per loaded state, capturing host kernel GS base and programming user-return registers, while the conventional variant also captures host segment selectors and bases and synchronizes nested control state if flagged.
Nested control synchronization chooses an enlightened copy when the enlightened pointer is valid and a shadow copy otherwise, then clears the pending synchronization flag.

Shadow copy iterates configured read-write and read-only field tables, reading each entry from the software copy and writing it into the loaded shadow control structure before restoring the previously loaded structure.

Enlightened copy transfers guest segment state, control registers, paging pointers, interrupt and exit info, and selected execution controls, while explicitly leaving host state and several bitmaps and addresses untouched.

Descriptor control updates race with concurrent outstanding-notification changes from other processors or devices, so failure of the atomic compare exchange must retry with a fresh snapshot rather than overwriting.

VCPU put dispatches by VCPU type; confidential put refreshes posted interrupt put handling and then prepares host state, while posted interrupt put arms a wakeup handler only for blocking non-preempted VCPUs with interrupts allowed and otherwise suppresses notifications.
Segment base resolution returns zero for null selectors, consults the current global table, and for local table selectors resolves the local table base recursively before indexing.
Notify-on-exit query reports enabled exactly when the per-VM architecture flag word has the designated enabled bit set.
Posted interrupt destination encoding uses the raw physical identifier in extended APIC mode and a shifted and masked eight bit field otherwise.
